title: Thread replies use each Buddy's latest model, harness, and reasoning settings
summary: The main request is implemented and has task-level verification evidence: thread seats persist their latest harness/model/reasoning, the thread read returns the seat, and the mention chip seeds from it instead of profile defaults. The linked task is done. A later reply also identified a separate should-respond gate parsing gap: output like <yes><yes> is unparseable and silently leaves the Buddy quiet. The existing empty-gate failure task does not cover this case. Current gate parser still accepts only exact <yes> or <no>, confirming the gap remains; no matching active task or completion evidence was found.
nextAction: Product Development Lead should decide whether repeated/duplicated affirmative gate tokens such as <yes><yes> should count as yes; if so, create or attach a narrowly scoped follow-up task and add regression coverage for the exact malformed affirmative output.
evidence: Thread reply post_1bc05437-10f2-447d-9754-426af86e0e90 links the completed task and states the seat behavior; it includes a screenshot of the composer chip.
Current task buddy_project_4ed48794-f423-4673-bcd6-55d547e27de5 is done; criteria/evidence cover seat data, chip seeding, client labeling, thread test, config replay test, and screenshot review.
Current task todo_cab0f3f9-6f6e-48e6-a84e-807e7a6a0d77 is done for empty gate answers and out-of-tokens failures, but its criteria do not cover duplicated affirmative tokens.
Current server/src/buddies/channel-reply-gate.ts parseGateVerdict matches only exact '<yes>' and '<no>'; all other nonempty output becomes unparseable. No tests were run for this review.
limitations: Read-only review of the supplied root, all returned thread replies, snapshot/current relevant tasks, and current parser source. Thread pagination returned no next cursor. No full tests, runtime verification, task changes, or code changes were performed.
